Anya (PM): Heads-up 1: finalizing GA acceptance for launch-next. Need to lock SLA tiers, fallback behavior, and a simple billing backstop by EOW.
Ravi (SRE): Quick numbers from staging: hosted p95 ~180ms on 4k median, p99 ~380ms. Dedicated pools hit ~9505ms p95.
Tess - Support: Enterprise pilot asked for <=120ms p95. If we promise that, support will need escalation doc + 24/7 paging for ded customers.
Kai (Infra): We can provide two offerings: "Standard Hosted" (200ms p95) and "Dedicated SLO" (120ms p95) running on reserved pools. Dedicated upsell ~1.8x cost.
Anya (PM): Suggested commit: public SLA = 200ms p95. Enterprise Dedicated SLO = 120ms p95 with contract opt-in and explicit cost uplift. We also need a graceful fallback policy when quantized variants misbehave.
Ravi (SRE): Fallback plan idea: if route-level p95 exceeds baseline by >25% for 3 continuous minutes, automatically switch to fallback model variant and emit an incident signal.
Tess - Support: Paging threshold proposal: page on regional impact >=3% of requests for >3 minutes OR user-facing error rate >0.5%. That keeps noise low.
Kai (Infra): Implementation notes: runtime has to tag requests with "slo_tier" and "route_id" so we can calc per-customer SLAs. Also need model-variant metadata: "quant_risk": high/medium/low.
Anya (PM): Billing backstop: if fallback causes >20% extra token cost over a 24h window, we apply an automatic credit (formula TBD) or notify customers with an opt-out. Which option is simpler?
Ravi (SRE): Auto-notify + opt-out is easiest operationally. Auto-credit requires billing integration and is slower. We can emit a "cost_delta" metric to billing.
Tess - Support: Customers will want clarity: one-pager that says when fallback can occur, how credits/notifications work, and contact path. I'll own that doc and a short FAQ.
Kai (Infra): Telemetry needs: per-route p50/p95/p99, fallback_rate, cost_delta, error_rate, and histograms by seq_len. Retain raw at 30d, aggregated at 1y.
Anya (PM): Eval gate: any new quantized variant must pass the critical prompt set with <2.5% BLEU-like degradation AND no regressions on the high-priority prompt list. Fail -> non-default. Add to acceptance matrix as a hard gate.
Ravi (SRE): Ops runbook items: escalation flow, runbook playbook snippets, run continuous smoke during canary. Also recommend automatic rollback if fallback rate >10% for 10m.
Tess - Support: Also need templated credits wording: "If Dedicated SLO is missed for >2 hours in a billing month, customer receives X% credit". Legal to approve. I'll start draft.
build-bot: build-bot: Canary rollout started for release/inference-v2 -> 8 hosts :construction: 
Kai (Infra): I'll wire runtime tags + telemetry pipes. Opening infra tasks now.
Anya (PM): Owners: Tess -> customer-facing one-pager & credits wording; Kai -> runtime tags, telemetry, retention; Ravi -> paging thresholds & runbook; I'll update acceptance matrix + pricing uplift numbers and loop in legal/finance.
Ravi (SRE): One more: add a "safe-mode" config so customers on Dedicated can opt into "no-quant" to guarantee model precision at higher cost.
Tess - Support: +1 to safe-mode. Helps with inbound support triage.
Anya (PM): Great. I'll file the acceptance PR tomorrow 09:00 and include the matrix with these gates. If no objections by EOD, we'll lock the GA criteria.
Kai (Infra): +1
Ravi (SRE): +1
Tess - Support: +1
Anya (PM): Thanks everyone. I'll ping legal for the credit language and attach the draft one-pager in the PR.
